Today is World Environment Day.
 
It is a reminder that every transition we build must stay within planetary boundaries. And AI is no exception.
 
Artificial intelligence will be shaped less by algorithms alone than by access to sustainable energy. By 2030, data centres are projected to consume nearly 945 TWh of electricity, with demand from AI-focused data centres expected to triple.
 
For developing countries, this creates a defining choice. AI could deepen existing inequalities, strain fragile energy systems and create new forms of dependency. Or it could open a green window of opportunity: helping countries strengthen clean power systems, build local capabilities and capture more value from the digital economy.
 
This is why an energy-ready AI future must place People, Planet and Prosperity at the centre:
 
👥 People: building skills, inclusion and public-interest digital infrastructure
 
🌱 Planet: powering AI with clean energy while reducing pressure on water, land and minerals
 
📈 Prosperity: creating local value, strengthening energy systems and enabling inclusive growth
 
I believe AI can support a just energy transition, but only if it is powered, governed and shaped for sustainable development.
